Finding a Roofer in Denton, Texas

Denton changed its roofing rules in 2022: every home re-roof now needs a city permit. Call one free number, any hour, and get connected with an independent roofing company that takes Denton calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 What the Denton roof permit checks
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Denton

A college town that rewrote its roofing rules

Hiring a roofer in Denton, TX means dealing with one of the more detailed re-roof processes in Denton County. Since June 1, 2022, the city has required a permit for every residential roof or re-roof project, not just new construction.

Denton is the county seat and, with 139,869 residents in the 2020 census, the 20th largest city in Texas. Two universities shaped it: the school that became the University of North Texas opened in 1890, and Texas Woman's University followed in 1901. Around them and the courthouse square sit some of the oldest houses in the county, while newer neighborhoods spread out from the interstates.

That mix shows up on roofs. A house near the square may sit in a historic district with its own review. A rental near campus may have a landlord deciding when the roof gets replaced. A newer house on the edge of town may just need its hail claim sorted out. DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a contractor: it connects you with an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Denton calls, and that company handles the permit.

What the Denton roof permit checks

The city's roofing page sets out more than a fee. These are the points a homeowner can see and ask about.

Permit before tear-off

The permit must be obtained before work starts, and the city counts tearing off the old roof as work. It should be posted where it can be seen from the street.

A registered contractor

The roofer registers with the city as a general contractor through eTRAKiT. First-time registration is done in person with photo ID, and it lasts one year.

Decking gets its own permit

If rotten or damaged decking is replaced, the city also requires a Residential Alteration Permit, and the decking is inspected before it is covered.

An attic look

Denton requires an attic interior inspection as part of the process. Plan for an inspector to need access to the attic hatch.

Drip edge on shingle roofs

Drip edge is required on asphalt shingle roofs. Ask the roofer to list it on the estimate so you know it is included.

A new material means review

Switching from shingles to metal, for example, triggers a plan review before approval. Solar panels pulled and reset need a licensed electrician named on the permit.

The October 2025 fee schedule lists the residential reroof permit at $50 and general contractor registration at $66. Development Services is at 401 N. Elm Street, (940) 349-8600. Confirm current fees with the city, since schedules change.

Houses in Oak-Hickory, West Oak and Bell Avenue

Denton has three local historic districts: Oak-Hickory, the West Oak Area and Bell Avenue. Inside them, and on any designated local landmark, Recorded Texas Historic Landmark or National Register landmark, the city requires a Certificate of Appropriateness before exterior repairs or alterations. Roofs are part of that, and past Historic Landmark Commission agendas include roof replacement requests.

The certificate must be approved before work begins, and a building permit is not issued until it is. The city's checklist says an application filed within two weeks of a Historic Landmark Commission meeting goes on the next meeting's agenda, and the commission generally meets once a month. In practice that means a roof replacement in one of these districts cannot always start the week the contract is signed. If your house is in a district, tell the roofer at the first visit, ask whether the material, color or profile is changing, and check with the city's historic preservation staff before you choose shingles.

What older Denton houses can hide

Houses built many decades ago were not always framed or decked the way a modern shingle roof expects. Some older homes carry more than one layer of roofing, or decking that needs replacing once the old layers come off. Nobody can price that from the driveway. Ask how the roofer will handle it if the deck turns out to be bad, how replacement boards are priced, and whether you will get photos before they are covered. In Denton that decking also needs its own permit and inspection, so it should never be a surprise line on the final bill.

Storms on record in Denton

Denton sits in the part of North Texas where spring supercells regularly drop large hail. Two events stand out in the official record:

DateWhat happened in DentonRoof concern
April 3, 2014The National Weather Service in Fort Worth logged 4.25 inch hail in Denton and an 82 mph gust at Denton Municipal Airport.Cracked and punctured shingles, broken vents and skylights, wind-lifted edges
April 30, 2019The NWS confirmed an EF-1 tornado with peak winds near 90 mph that first touched down near the Texas Woman's University campus. A second EF-1 struck east of Justin the same evening.Torn shingles, lifted decking, tree limbs on roofs

Hail of that size can damage a roof in ways that are hard to see from the ground. If a storm passes and you are unsure, a roof inspection gives you something concrete to take to your insurer. Keep in mind that only you and your insurance company settle the claim.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Denton Municipal Electric through city dispatch at (940) 349-7000 if you are a DME customer, or to the utility named on your bill, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Six questions for a Denton roofer

  • Under what business name are you registered with the City of Denton, and is that registration current?
  • Will the permit be issued before tear-off, and where will you post it?
  • If decking needs replacing, will you add the Residential Alteration Permit and show me photos?
  • Is drip edge on this estimate?
  • Is my house in Oak-Hickory, West Oak or Bell Avenue, and who files the Certificate of Appropriateness?
  • For a rental: will the owner or the property manager sign the contract and receive the warranty paperwork?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

What Denton homeowners ask about roofers

Do you need a permit to replace a roof in Denton, TX?

Yes. Since June 1, 2022, the City of Denton has required a roof permit for all residential roof and re-roof projects, and the permit has to be issued before tear-off starts. If decking is replaced, a Residential Alteration Permit is needed as well. The October 2025 fee schedule lists the residential reroof permit at $50. Questions go to Development Services at (940) 349-8600.

How can I tell if a Denton roofing company is registered with the city?

Denton requires the company to register as a general contractor through the city's eTRAKiT system, and registrations expire a year after they are issued. Ask for the exact business name on the registration and make sure it matches your contract and the permit. Texas has no state roofing license, so this city step matters. Our guide to checking a roofer covers the rest.

My house is in the Oak-Hickory district. Can I just put on a new roof?

Not without a step first. Denton requires a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior repairs and alterations in its local historic districts (Oak-Hickory, West Oak Area and Bell Avenue) and on designated landmarks. The certificate has to be approved before work begins, and the city will not issue a building permit until it is. Applications filed within two weeks of a Historic Landmark Commission meeting wait for the following meeting, so ask the city early and build that time into the roofer's schedule.

Who do I call about a power line on my roof in Denton?

Keep well back from it, and dial 911 if someone could be hurt. Much of Denton is served by the city's own utility, Denton Municipal Electric, and the city asks people to report downed poles or wires to its dispatch line, (940) 349-7000. Parts of Denton County are served by other providers, so check the name on your electric bill. A roofer should not start until the line is safe.

Is DFW Expert Roofers a Denton roofing company?

No. It is a free phone line. An automated assistant answers any hour, asks about the roof and your town, then transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that serves Denton. That company sees the roof, writes the estimate, pulls the city permit and does the work, and you pay it directly. The line may receive a referral fee. How a call is handled.
